name: Revolutionary nationalism
summary: Revolutionary nationalism is a label for nationalist movements that pursue independence or national renewal by overthrowing the existing order, typically through armed struggle against colonial or foreign domination. In its mainstream anti-colonial form it ties political independence to economic transformation, mass participation and a people's right to its own history and culture, usually with a socialist or anti-imperialist orientation.
scope: Revolutionary nationalism as the anti-colonial national-liberation current of the 20th century, centred on Amilcar Cabral, whom the scholarship (s5, reviewing Rabaka) calls a revolutionary nationalist, with Frantz Fanon's work as the context s5 names: nationalism pursued by revolution against colonial or neocolonial rule and joined to a social transformation toward decolonial democratic socialism. Other movements that Wikipedia's overview lists under the label (Irish Fenians, Sandino, the Bolivian MNR, the Indian independence revolutionaries, Eritrea, the French Revolution, Italian Fascism, Third Positionists) are not scoped in because no defining source saved here states their positions; because the label is descriptive rather than one doctrine, the answers follow the left anti-colonial strand and many are low-confidence.
